@Tatiana Mirson could you, please, change the border of the dialog to "CanvasText" (would appear white on this theme)? the dialog itself is not interactive, thus button color is not needed :)

Also re: QR code (optional):
to make sure it does appear in the styles that are easy for the user's eyes, we could make the colors:
* white to "CanvasText" (would appear white on this theme and would use whatever color the user is set to their text)
* black to "Canvas" (would appear black on this theme and would use whatever color the user is set to their background that is used with text)
While it won't be always black and white, there would be still a color contrast that is expected to be readable by the user - thus would/should work for the camera too. I.e. a popular low contrast (dark) theme Gotham would have lighter turquoise text and dark blue background, it is still readable - and would still be picked up by a more-less okay camera.

Example with the Gotham colors worked well on both not-very-recent iPhone and Android. This theme is an edge case when a user would have to explicitly set those lower-than-usual contrasted colors to be their main colors for any text. But it would still work. And the QR code won't be "stinging" this user's eyes as if may if it appears black-on-white on their low HCM theme.

@Tatiana Mirson We need to follow the visual reading order and have the "Cancel" be item #2 and "Submit" the last one - item #3. Especially, because the Submit would be disabled > not focusable and the user would need to know they have to navigate backwards to get to it. Rule of thumb is to follow the visual reading order since keyboard users are sighted users too and it is the predictable/expected order

Also, I updated the numbers in the annotations to use letters for landmarks and numbers for keyboard focusable elements, so it's also easy to check in the build that the first item focused is the item #1 (1a in this case)
